title: 417. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Quotient and Reciprocal Identities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: State tangent as a quotient of sine and cosine.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\tan\theta\) equals which quotient?
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, \(\tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}\) with \(y=\sin\theta\) and \(x=\cos\theta\), so \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\). The reversed quotient \(\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\) is \(\cot\theta\).
questions.hint: In a right triangle, divide the sine ratio by the cosine ratio and see which sides remain.

questions.learningObjective: State cotangent as a quotient of cosine and sine.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\cot\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: The cotangent is the reciprocal of the tangent: \(\cot\theta=\frac{1}{\tan\theta}=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\). The expression \(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\) is \(\sec\theta\).
questions.hint: Take the reciprocal of the quotient that defines tangent.

questions.learningObjective: State secant as the reciprocal of cosine.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\sec\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: By definition, the secant is the reciprocal of the cosine: \(\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\). The reciprocal of the sine is \(\csc\theta\), the cosecant.
questions.hint: Secant pairs with cosine, and cosecant pairs with sine.

questions.concept: Tangent from decimal sine and cosine
questions.learningObjective: Compute a tangent from given sine and cosine values.
questions.question: For an angle \(\theta\), \(\sin\theta=0.6\) and \(\cos\theta=0.8\). What is \(\tan\theta\)?
questions.explanation: By the quotient identity, \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{0.6}{0.8}=0.75\). The value \(1.25\) is \(\frac{1}{0.8}\), which is \(\sec\theta\), not \(\tan\theta\).
questions.hint: Divide the sine by the cosine.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a product by writing tangent as a quotient.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\tan\theta\cos\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Replace \(\tan\theta\) by \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\): \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\cdot\cos\theta=\sin\theta\). The factor \(\cos\theta\) cancels; it does not move into the denominator.
questions.hint: Write tangent as sine over cosine and cancel the common factor.

questions.concept: Product of a function and its reciprocal
questions.learningObjective: Simplify the product of sine and cosecant.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\sin\theta\csc\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Since \(\csc\theta=\frac{1}{\sin\theta}\), \(\sin\theta\csc\theta=\sin\theta\cdot\frac{1}{\sin\theta}=1\). The expression \(\sin^2\theta\) would result from multiplying sine by itself, not by its reciprocal.
questions.hint: Replace cosecant by its definition in terms of sine.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a product by writing cotangent as a quotient.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\cot\theta\sin\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Replace \(\cot\theta\) by \(\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\): \(\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\cdot\sin\theta=\cos\theta\). The result is the cosine itself, not its reciprocal \(\sec\theta\).
questions.hint: Write cotangent as cosine over sine and cancel.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a quotient of two reciprocal functions.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\frac{\sec\theta}{\csc\theta}\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Rewrite with sine and cosine: \(\frac{\sec\theta}{\csc\theta}=\frac{1/\cos\theta}{1/\sin\theta}=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\tan\theta\). Dividing by a fraction multiplies by its reciprocal, so the sine ends up in the numerator.
questions.hint: Convert both functions to sine and cosine, then divide the fractions.

questions.learningObjective: Rearrange the quotient identity to find a sine.
questions.question: An angle \(\theta\) has \(\tan\theta=\frac{3}{4}\) and \(\cos\theta=-\frac{4}{5}\). What is \(\sin\theta\)?
questions.explanation: From \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\), \(\sin\theta=\tan\theta\cos\theta=\frac{3}{4}\cdot\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)=-\frac{3}{5}\). A positive tangent with a negative cosine places \(\theta\) in Quadrant III, where the sine is indeed negative.
questions.hint: Multiply both sides of the quotient identity by \(\cos\theta\) and keep the sign.

questions.learningObjective: Combine quotient identities over a common denominator.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\tan\theta+\cot\theta\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Write both terms with sine and cosine: \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=\frac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\). By the reciprocal identities this is \(\sec\theta\csc\theta\). The product \(\sin\theta\cos\theta\) is the denominator, not the value.
questions.hint: Convert to sine and cosine, add the fractions with a common denominator, and simplify the numerator.
